facts.statement: Pulanesaura lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically from the late Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, in what is now South Africa.
facts.quote: Pulanesaura is an extinct genus of basal sauropodiform known from the Early Jurassic (late Hettangian to Sinemurian) Upper Elliot Formation of the Free State, South Africa.

facts.statement: Fossils of Pulanesaura were discovered in 2004 by paleontologist Matthew Bonnan at a quarry on the Spion Kop 932 farm in the Free State, South Africa.
facts.quote: The remains of Pulanesaura were discovered in a small quarry in the farm Spion Kop 932 in the Senekal District of the Free State in 2004 by paleontologist Matthew Bonnan.

facts.statement: The genus Pulanesaura and its type species Pulanesaura eocollum were formally described in 2015 by a team including Blair W. McPhee and Matthew F. Bonnan.
facts.quote: Pulanesaura was then described and named officially by Blair W. McPhee, Matthew F. Bonnan, Adam M. Yates, Johann Neveling and Jonah N. Choiniere in 2015 with the type species Pulanesaura eocollum.

facts.statement: The genus name Pulanesaura combines the Sesoth word 'Pulane' (rain-maker) and the Latin suffix 'saura' (lizard), referencing the heavy rain conditions during discovery.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Sesoth word for "rain-maker/bringer", Pulane, in reference to the heavy rain conditions under which the remains were collected, and the feminine form of the common dinosaur name suffix, saura, meaning "lizard" in Latin.

facts.statement: The species name 'eocollum' means 'dawn neck', highlighting that this basal sauropod lacked the extremely long necks seen in later sauropods.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Greek eo, meaning "dawn", and Latin collum, meaning "neck", in reference to Pulanesaura being a very basal sauropod not yet showing the most archetypal trait of more advanced sauropods - their very long necks.

facts.statement: The known fossil material of Pulanesaura includes partial skeletons of at least two individuals ranging from subadult to adult size.
facts.quote: Pulanesaura is known from partial remains of at least two subadult to adult individuals.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as BP/1/6982, consists of a front dorsal vertebra missing the tip of its neural spine.
facts.quote: The holotype, BP/1/6982, represents the front dorsal vertebra missing the tip of the neural spine.

facts.statement: Referred material includes various bones such as teeth, vertebrae, ribs, a clavicle, limb bones, and claws, found in close association with the holotype.
facts.quote: In addition the referred material consists of two isolated teeth, a middle cervical vertebra, five back vertebral arches, a single right dorsal rib, three tail vertebrae, a left clavicle, a distal right humerus, a left ulna, possibly the fourth right middle hand bone, three ischia, a left and a right shinbones, and two hindlimb first claws.

facts.statement: Pulanesaura's skeletal structure suggests it was a low browser, feeding on vegetation close to the ground unlike other prosauropods in its environment.
facts.quote: Pulanesauras posture and skeletal build indicate that the animal was a low browser, unlike the prosauropods it shared its habitat with.

facts.statement: Pulanesaura possessed a flexible neck that allowed it to feed efficiently with minimal body movement, a trait later exaggerated in advanced sauropods.
facts.quote: Its flexible neck would have further allowed it to feed without moving its body very often and expending valuable energy; a trait that later sauropods would take to extreme lengths.

facts.statement: Pulanesaura lived in an arid floodplain environment where vegetation was concentrated around river channels, allowing it to coexist with other sauropodomorphs like Aardonyx and Arcusaurus.
facts.quote: Studies of the Upper Elliot Formation suggest that the environment was a predominantly arid floodplain where vegetation was concentrated most heavily around the river channels that flowed through the area, further allowing the coexistence of Pulanesaura with other sauropodomorphs such as Aardonyx and Arcusaurus.

facts.statement: Pulanesaura is classified as a medium-sized transitional sauropodiform.
facts.quote: Pulanesaura es un sauropodiforme transicional de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pulanesaura should be classified as one of the least derived sauropods or as the sister taxon to Sauropoda, depending on whether a node-based or stem-based definition of Sauropoda is applied.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético encontró que podría ser clasificado como uno de los saurópodos menos derivados o bien podría ser un taxón hermano de Sauropoda, dependiendo de la definición filogenética usada para Sauropoda (basada en nodos o en tallos).

facts.statement: Pulanesaura was a low-level browser, unlike the prosauropods that shared its habitat.
facts.quote: La postura de Pulanesaura y la constitución de su esqueleto indican que el animal era un ramoneador de nivel bajo, a diferencia de los prosaurópodos con los que compartía su hábitat.

facts.statement: Studies by Blair McPhee et al. indicate that Pulanesaura coexisted with other sauropodomorphs in the same formation through ecological niche differentiation.
facts.quote: Los estudios realizados por Blair McPhee et al. indican que Pulanesaura coexistía con los otros sauropodomorfos hallados en la misma formación gracias a la diferenciación de nichos ecológicos.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that its flexible neck allowed it to feed without frequently moving its body, conserving valuable energy.
facts.quote: Su cuello flexible le pudo haber permitido alimentarse sin mover su cuerpo de manera frecuente y evitando gastar energía valiosa

facts.statement: Pulanesaura belongs to the parent group Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropoda

facts.statement: Pulanesaura is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Pulanesaura lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Pulanesaura was named by McPhee et al. in 2015.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Pulanesaura (genus), McPhee et al. 2015

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Pulanesaura in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
